qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Unassailable global monopoly in cystic fibrosis (CF) transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators (Trikafta/Kaftrio, Alyftrek). Decades of structural biology and medicinal chemistry patents protect the franchise through 2037 (Trikafta) and 2039+ (vanzacaftor triple). Inelastic pricing power demonstrated by universal Western reimbursement at ~$300k+/patient/year with zero clinical churn. 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 59.6% and operating ROIC of 90.5% provide empirical proof of moat. Primary long-term erosion risk is eventual 2037+ patent expirations and nascent genetic curative therapies.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Unrivaled biopharmaceutical monopoly in cystic fibrosis with patent protection extending into late 2030s, complemented by pipeline expansion into non-opioid pain (Suzetrigine) and gene-edited cell therapies (Casgevy). Debt-free fortress balance sheet with >$5B in cash and marketable securities and 50%+ normalized ROIC. [5-10Y g: CF global patient penetration 3.0% + Alyftrek vanzacaftor upgrade 2.0% + Suzetrigine pain launch 2.5% - R&D reinvestment drag 0.5% + net share repurchases 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: 10-year financial record demonstrates extraordinary compounding: revenue expanded from $1.7B in 2016 to $12.0B in 2025, with operating EBIT rising from $10M to $4.17B. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 59.64% with tangible ROIC of 90.48%. FCF conversion exceeds 80% over multi-year cycles (2025 FCF of $3.19B vs Net Income of $3.95B; 2024 dip was driven solely by a one-off non-deductible $4.4B AIPR&D accounting charge for the Alpine Immune Sciences acquisition). Peak Owner EPS reached a new high of $15.32 in FY2025. Balance sheet carries zero long-term funded debt ($0.0M) and over $5.08B in cash and marketable securities. Commercial CFTR treatments face zero direct competition across ~90% of addressable CF patients globally.
